name: Sibutramine
lead: Sibutramine, sold as Meridia (US) and Reductil (elsewhere), is a serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor that was approved as an appetite suppressant for obesity and later withdrawn from major markets over cardiovascular safety concerns [1][2]. Randomised trials found it produced modest weight loss beyond diet and exercise [3][4].

The 2010 SCOUT outcomes trial in more than 10,000 overweight or obese people with cardiovascular disease or diabetes led regulators to suspend or withdraw it [5][6]. Looksmaxxing relevance is limited: the sources show only scattered mentions on bodybuilding forums such as T Nation, where users compared it with ECA stacks and other appetite suppressants before and after withdrawal [7][8]. Sibutramine is also known as an undeclared ingredient in some weight-loss supplements [1].

paras: Sibutramine was approved by the FDA in November 1997 for adults with a BMI of 30 or higher, or 27 or higher with comorbid conditions, in addition to diet and exercise [1]. An obesity-guideline from endocrinologists and a systematic review of emerging obesity drugs place it among historical pharmacotherapies [9][10]. A US trial registry lists a study in binge-eating disorder and trials in adolescents [11][12].

Randomised placebo-controlled trials in the 1990s found dose-related weight loss [3][4][13]. A general reference reports about 4.5 kg greater loss than placebo at one year in meta-analytic data [1]. The STORM study followed participants for two years after initial weight loss and compared continued treatment with placebo [14]. Reviews of weight-loss trials with at least one year of follow-up and a meta-analysis of long-term pharmacotherapy included sibutramine [15][16].

Commonly reported effects include dry mouth, insomnia, constipation and raised heart rate and blood pressure [1]. A case report described a psychotic episode associated with sibutramine [17]. The SCOUT trial enrolled 10,744 participants aged 55 or older with cardiovascular disease, diabetes or both to assess cardiovascular outcomes with and without sibutramine [5]. A general reference reports a 16 percent relative increase in non-fatal heart attack or stroke versus placebo [1].

Sibutramine inhibits reuptake of serotonin and norepinephrine, with a weaker effect on dopamine, increasing satiety [1]. It is metabolised to active desmethyl metabolites; the primary active metabolite has a half-life of about 14 hours [1]. Studies have also examined its effect on norepinephrine transporter activity in tilt-induced presyncope [18].

Boots Pharmaceuticals in Nottingham developed sibutramine (BTS 54524) in the 1980s as an antidepressant candidate, and animal studies showing reduced food intake redirected it toward obesity [1]. It was approved by the FDA on 22 November 1997 and sold from 1998 [1]. After SCOUT, the European Medicines Agency suspended it in January 2010, and the FDA requested withdrawal in October 2010 [1][6].

subs.h: Use in looksmaxxing and fitness communities
paras: T Nation threads have discussed sibutramine alongside ECA stacks, phentermine and other appetite suppressants, with one 2009 thread asking about Meridia versus an ECA stack after a doctor suggested it [7][8]. One forum user listed it among pharmaceutical options for combined appetite suppression and warned of side effects [8]. A 2010 T Nation thread on government regulation of supplements also touched on it [19]. No looksmax.org discussion of it was found.

Human studies are extensive. SCOUT, a randomised trial of 10,744 high-risk participants, assessed cardiovascular outcomes [5]. STORM examined weight maintenance after weight loss in a two-year randomised design [14]. Earlier randomised trials found dose-related weight loss [3][13]. Meta-analyses of obesity drugs also include it [15][16][20]. Registered trials examined sibutramine in adolescents, in binge-eating disorder, and with metformin [11][12][21].

timeline.event: Boots develops sibutramine, originally as an antidepressant [1].
SCOUT results published; EMA suspends and FDA requests withdrawal [5][6].

lore.intro: Within bodybuilding forums sibutramine is mentioned as a former prescription appetite suppressant, discussed beside ECA stacks and other stimulants [7][8].

claims.claim: Sibutramine is a strong appetite suppressant that can substitute for or complement an ECA stack.
claims.believers: T Nation members raised it as an option compared with ephedrine stacks when dieting [7][8].
claims.experts: Randomised trials found dose-related weight loss, with about 4.5 kg more than placebo at one year according to a general reference [3][1].

claims.claim: Combining appetite suppressants and other agents improves fat loss.
claims.believers: One forum post suggested that combining medications with different modes of action produces better results, while acknowledging side effects [8].
claims.experts: No published trial tested such combinations for physique purposes; registered trials have examined sibutramine with metformin in obesity [21].

claims.claim: Sibutramine remains safe to use outside medical supervision.
claims.believers: Community threads found do not make this claim directly.
claims.experts: The SCOUT trial led to its withdrawal from the EU and US in 2010 [5][6].

card.summary: A withdrawn prescription appetite suppressant that worked modestly for weight loss but raised cardiovascular risk in high-risk patients.
card.note: Withdrawn in the EU and US in 2010 after the SCOUT cardiovascular trial; undeclared in some supplements.

quick.overview:
Sibutramine was a prescription weight-loss pill that made people feel full sooner. Trials showed it helped people lose a few kilograms more than diet alone.

It was withdrawn in 2010 after a large trial in high-risk patients found more heart attacks and strokes. It has little presence in looksmaxxing forums.
quick.mechanism: It blocks reuptake of serotonin and norepinephrine in the brain, increasing feelings of fullness and reducing food intake.
quick.risks: Reported effects include raised heart rate and blood pressure, dry mouth, insomnia and constipation, and a case report of psychosis. Regulators withdrew it in the EU and US in 2010.
